 Dated this the 7th day of February, 2025  JUDGMENT 1.

The petitioner entered the service to the Kerala Financial Corporation on 10.02.2014 in the entry cadre of Assistant under the die-in harness scheme, and he was promoted to the post of Junior Executive on 10.02.2017.

2. One Shri. Alexander John, an A-class Contractor, approached the respondent Corporation for a loan under the Scheme of Line of Credit (LOC) for the Contractors, and the respondent Corporation sanctioned the payment of Rs. 500 Lakhs on 23.12.2019.

Rs.308.23 Lakhs was allotted from the sanctioned amount of Rs.500 Lakhs as Work Execution Facility (WEF) to execute the contract work for the development of TS Canal from Ch:49740m to Ch:50900m at Varkala with an agreed PAC of Rs.385.29 Lakhs.

3. A Power of Attorney was executed by the Contractor on 30.11.2019 in favour of the respondent Corporation, authorising the Corporation to receive the bill amount of the work carried out in 2025:KER:10387 respect of the said contract work.
As a security of the said loan, the contractor had mortgaged 17.90 Ares of land in Revenue Survey No. 11/5 Melila Village with a residential building thereon owned by his wife.
4. The petitioner was placed under suspension on 10.03.2021.

The incident which led to the suspension of the petitioner was that on 17.01.2021, the son of the Contractor submitted the stage certificate received from the office of the Assistant Engineer, Irrigation Department, Inland Navigation Section, Varkala dated 11.01.2021 to the petitioner, who was the present officer handling the loan.

sentences.text: The petitioner uploaded the stage certificate submitted by the son of the contractor in the Contractor Loan Module of CFS (software handling contractor loans) on 20.01.2021, mentioning that 85% (modifying 35% as 85%) of the work was completed.
The petitioner also uploaded site inspection report dated 14.01.2021 stating that he had visited the work site and 85% physical achievement of work was completed.

Based on this manipulated stage certificate and petitioner's inspection report uploaded in the system, the Chief Manager of the KFC Kollam branch office approved the release of funds, and Corporation released an amount of Rs.153 Lakhs on 2025:KER:10387 21.01.2021 to the Contractor.

The Contractor, Sri. Alexander John expired on 13.02.2021.
6.

It appears that the Chief Manager (CM), Branch Office, Kollam had a discussion with the son of late Alexander John regarding the progress of work at the site and deputed Smt. Leena Prasad,
Junior Technical Officer (JTO) to inspect the site.

Smt. Leena Prasad reported on 03.03.2021 that physical progress of the work was only 15%.
7.

After receiving the report from Smt. Leena Prasad, son of late Alexander John was called to the Office on the next day to clarify the disparity between the stage certificate and actual progress of work.

He informed that the physical progress of the work was only 35% and the stage completion certificate received from the department showed only 35% which was forwarded by him to the petitioner on behalf of his father for release of the next installment of the loan.
8. It appears that there was manipulation of 35% to 85%.

Though in site inspection the progress was shown only 15% but, the petitioner reported that the progress of work was around 85% and on the basis of the report submitted by the petitioner, Rs. 153.00 2025:KER:10387 lakhs were released in favour of the Contractor.

9. An FIR came to be registered under Sections 409,420,464, 468, 471, 477A and 34 of IPC at Kollam East Police Station in respect of the manipulation and false certificate submitted by the petitioner.
The petitioner is one of the accused in the said FIR in which charge sheet has been submitted.
It is stated at the Bar that the case is posted for framing of the charges.

The petitioner was issued charge memo in Exhibit P-1 having four charges as follows;
Charge 1: You have forged the stage certificate showing the percentage of completion of work from 35% to 85% with malafide intention of reporting exaggerated progress of work for disbursing higher amount to the loanee.
For this you have obtained a sum of Rs. 150,000/- from late Sri. Alexander John on 21.08.2020 to your SB account maintained with Federal Bank, Paravoor branch.
Shri. Jins Alex has informed that he had forwarded the stage certificate of 35% issued by Inland Navigation Section, Varkala to your official e-mail id on 17.01.2021.
On 09.03.2021 the mail sent to you by Shri.
Jins Alex was forwarded to CM, KFC Kollam in which it was clearly noted that physical progress of the work was only 35% in the stage certificate issued by the Inland Navigation Section, Varkala.
Charge 2: You have uploaded the forged stage certificate and false inspection report where physical progress of the work was shown as 85% in contractor loan module of CFS on 20.01.2021.

You have informed that you inspected the site on 14.01.2021 which was actually a local public holiday for Kollam District due to Thaipponkal and reported that the physical achievement of this work is 85%

3 and uploaded the fake site inspection report on 20.01.2021 in CFS.

Thus it is clear that you have not 2025:KER:10387 visited the site and you prepared a fake site visit report only after 17.01.2021 and not on 14.01.2021 which was actually a local public holiday for Kollam District due to Thaipponkal.
Charge 3: Based on the stage certificate and your inspection report uploaded in system Corporation has released second instalment of loan amounting to Rs. 153 lakh on 21.01.2021.
Thus the total disbursement in the loan comes to Rs. 272.45 lakh.

It is clear that fraud committed by you regarding the stage certificate and fake inspection report has resulted in excess release of funds by the corporation and prima-face case of intentionally causing financial loss to the Corporation.

The Enquiry Officer submitted the report in Exhibit P-12 on 31.03.2022 finding that all the four charges mentioned above against the petitioner proved.
The petitioner was issued the show cause notice along with the enquiry report for which he replied.
Before a 2025:KER:10387 decision would be taken on enquiry report by the disciplinary authority, the petitioner has approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.
This Court vide the order dated 10.05.2022 stayed all further proceedings.

11. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was acting upon the instructions of his senior and the petitioner does not have the power to sanction the loan and he was bound by the instructions.
He further submits that the District Manager was the sanctioning authority.
The petitioner was not the prime accused in the FIR and initiation of the disciplinary proceedings against the petitioner is wholly untenable.

12. On the other hand, Ms. Danya P. Asokan, the learned Senior Counsel for the respondent Corporation submits that the fact remains that the petitioner has been found guilty in respect of all the four charges by the Enquiry Officer.
The petitioner was issued show cause notice at this stage interdicting the disciplinary proceedings without final order is not justified.

She further submits that the petitioner cannot deny that he is an accused for an offence in respect of which FIR No. 0437 of 2021 has been registered and charge sheet 2025:KER:10387 has been submitted on 15.02.2023 and the case is posted for framing of the charges.

She further submits that, considering the allegation against the petitioner and the enquiry report, this Court should not interfere with the ongoing disciplinary proceedings against the petitioner and the writ petition is liable to be dismissed.
13. I have considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the learned Counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent Corporation.
Charges against the petitioner is serious which may attract the penalty of dismissal from service.
The Enquiry Officer has found all the four charges proved against the petitioner.

At this stage, disciplinary proceedings Ajithsen vs The Kerala Financial Corporation on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66170845/
5 cannot be interdicted.

sentences.text: I do not find any substance in the submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioner that the findings recorded by the Enquiry Officer will prejudice the trial.
14. In criminal trial, the charge is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt where in disciplinary proceedings it is only a preponderance of probability which is required to be proved.
There is no law which prohibits or bars the disciplinary proceedings till conclusion of the trial in criminal case.
The scope of enquiry in criminal cases as well as 2025:KER:10387 disciplinary proceedings is different in quality and the evidence.
The enquiry report in which the petitioner has been found guilty of the four charges as mentioned above cannot be said that it would prejudice the petitioner's trial in the criminal case.
15. In view thereof, I do not find that this writ petition has merit and this Court should interdict the final order to be passed by the disciplinary authority.
Thus, the present writ petition is hereby dismissed.
However, the petitioner should be given an opportunity of hearing by the disciplinary authority before taking the final decision on the enquiry report submitted by the enquiry officer.
Interim order dated10.05.2022 stands vacated.
